Go's os.Root: what it does and does not give you (Go 1.26.6 doc)

Confines every method to the directory; follows symlinks but refuses ones that escape or are absolute; on Windows also rejects reserved device names and treats junctions as symlinks. It does not stop bind mounts or /proc, and Chmod/Chown/Chtimes race against a file-to-symlink swap on Unix — so set perms on the open file (f.Chmod, as the branch's writer now does), never by path. Every helper in safefile should carry that list in its doc comment so call sites stop re-deriving it.

User settings file: schema and precedence

One file, ~/.config/entire/settings.json, hand-editable, documented as stable. Blocks are independent so a block can be strict without the file being brittle.

{
  // exists today on feat/global-trust — unchanged
  "global": {
    "enabled": true,
    "exclude_paths": ["~/scratch/**"],
    "trust_all": false,
    "trusted_origins": ["github.com/entireio/cli"]
  },

  // NEW — how OPF runs on THIS machine. "enabled"/"categories" stay in the
  // team's .entire/settings.json (what to redact is policy; how to run it is local).
  "redaction": {
    "openai_privacy_filter": {
      "command": "/opt/homebrew/bin/opf",
      "timeout_seconds": 120,
      "prompt_default": "ask"
    }
  },

  // NEW — machine-wide developer defaults (were per-worktree in settings.local.json)
  "review_profiles": { "quick": { "agent": "claude-code", "skills": ["/review"] } },
  "review_default_profile": "quick",
  "investigate": { "agents": ["claude-code", "codex"], "max_turns": 2 },
  "summary_generation": { "provider": "claude-code" },

  // NEW — per-repository overrides, keyed like trusted_origins
  "repos": {
    "github.com/entireio/cli": {
      "review_default_profile": "pr-toolkit",
      "review_profiles": { "pr-toolkit": { "agent": "claude-code", "skills": ["/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr"] } },
      "strategy_options": { "checkpoint_remote": { "provider": "github", "repo": "peyton-alt/cli-checkpoints" } }
    },
    // no-origin repos key by canonical path, same rule as trusted_paths
    "/Users/me/code/notes": { "review_default_profile": "quick" }
  }
}

Decode rule

  • Top level: tolerant. Unknown top-level keys are kept as json.RawMessage, round-tripped on write, and reported once by entire doctor ("key foo is not understood by this version"). This is what lets a 0.11 binary and a 0.12 binary share a machine.
  • Inside global and redaction: strict, fail that block closed — exactly #2030's current behaviour, scoped to the blocks where an unrecognized key could mean an unrecognized exclusion or an unrecognized command option.
  • Inside preferences blocks (review_*, investigate, summary_generation, repos.*): strict on the known struct, but a failure drops the block with a warning rather than the file. Losing a review preference must never disable tracking.

Precedence (lowest → highest)

  1. <worktree>/.entire/settings.json — team
  2. User file, top-level blocks — me, every repo
  3. User file, repos["<key>"] — me, this repo, every worktree of every clone
  4. <worktree>/.entire/settings.local.json — me, this worktree only. Kept for what is genuinely per-worktree (enabled for enable --local, an experiment in one checkout). Exec-bearing keys are no longer read from here.

Consent stays where #2030 put it: global.trust_* is the only egress switch, a committed enabled: false still vetoes, and nothing in the repository can open the sync path. The per-repo checkpoint_remote moving to the user tier actually strengthens CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly: "the developer chose this remote" becomes a fact about which file it came from, with no tracked-file probe needed.

Migration 1 — OPF out of the worktree

Smallest useful slice; ships independently of #2030 landing, because the user file's loader can be lifted into settings on its own.

  1. Loader. settings.Load reads the user file after the project file and before the local file. enforceOPFCommandTrust gains a first case: command came from the user file → accept, no probe. The existing local-file path stays for one release.
  2. Deprecate the local path. When command is found in settings.local.json, honor it (probe and all) but print once per day: "OPF command is read from ~/.config/entire/settings.json from v0.13; run entire configure --opf-command <path> to move it." entire doctor lists the file and the fix.
  3. Remove. Next minor: drop the local-file case, delete classifyLocalSettingsDeep and the HEAD probe. The shallow index probe remains only until the local layer stops being a security input at all (it still gates CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly today; that goes with Migration 2).
  4. Windows. The command is exec'd directly (never via cmd.exe, per CLAUDE.md); accept opf.exe, paths with spaces, and %LOCALAPPDATA%-style values only if expanded by the user's shell — do not expand env vars in the setting. Reject a relative command (it would resolve against the repo CWD) unless it is a bare name resolved on PATH with exec.ErrDot protection, as today.
  5. Docs. docs/security-and-privacy.md "Why command is local-only" becomes "Why command is user-only" — the argument gets shorter, which is the point.

What this buys: one OPF setting per machine instead of per worktree; the pre-push trust gate no longer reads the git index or HEAD; the exec boundary is expressible in one sentence ("Entire only executes what ~/.config/entire names").

Migration 2 — dissolving preferences.json

The file has three kinds of content; each has a better home. Once they move, ClonePreferences and its loader delete outright.

ContentLifetimeMove toWhy
review_profiles, review_default_profile, legacy review, review_fix_agentDurable preferenceuser repos["<key>"].review_*, falling back to top-level review_*Survives re-clone; shared across clones and worktrees; the picker writes one place. The one-shot migration prompt in review/picker.go already knows how to move keys between files — point it at the new destination.
review_migration_dismissedDurable flaguser top-levelA user's answer, not a clone's.
trails_enabled*, trails_agent_help_*1 h cache / 5 min backoffuser ~/.cache/entire/repos/<key>/trails.jsonAlready keyed by repo_key + api_base + auth_key — user-scoped by construction. No git rev-parse on the write path; one answer per repo per machine; safe to delete; entire clean can sweep it.
GlobalSetupCompleted (feat/global-writer)Stampclone <git-common>/entire/…It records that this clone was set up; #2030's later heads already replaced it with the derived primary-ref-ready stamp in the runtime root.

Order of work

  1. Trails cache first — it is a cache, so the migration is "start writing the new location, stop reading the old". Zero user-visible change.
  2. Review prefs second, behind the existing picker migration prompt: on first entire review with a populated preferences.json, copy into repos["<key>"] and rename the old file to preferences.json.migrated. Read the old file as a fallback for one release.
  3. Delete ClonePreferences, applyClonePreferences, and the preferencesFileAbs parameter of loadMergedSettings. settings.Load stops shelling out to git rev-parse --git-common-dir on every call (it does today, via clonePreferencesPathForWorktreeRoot, purely to find this file).

Repo key for repos without an origin

Reuse #2030's TrustIdentity rule exactly: origin present and every fetch/push URL normalizes → keyed by host/owner/repo; otherwise keyed by canonical worktree path. One rule, already documented, already tested for Windows drive letters and case folding.

Migration 3 — logs and tmp

Three candidate homes for .entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}; the choice is about layout, not trust, since all three are Entire-owned and gitignored or outside the tree.

A · Keep <worktree>/.entire/… for repo-enabled repos (status quo)

No migration; doctor bundle and docs unchanged. Cost: two layouts to reason about once #2030 lands (global repos use B), and the runtime dir sits inside a tree the repository controls, so it needs the #2154/#2156 guard forever.

B · <git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/… for every active repo ← recommended

#2030 already builds this for global mode; adopting it for local mode gives one layout, one os.Root anchor, byte-clean git status in every repo, and takes runtime data out of the repository-controlled tier. Cost: a one-time move of existing logs (or just start fresh — full.jsonl is regenerated per Stop), and the temp file for an atomic write must be on the same filesystem as its destination (it will be — same .git).

C · ~/.local/state/entire/repos/<key>/… (XDG state; %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows)

Right for logs that are not about one repo (login, version check, the future session-binding records currently in ~/.config/entire/sessions/). Wrong for metadata/tmp: hooks would write across filesystems, and two clones of one repo would collide on the key.

So: B for repo runtime, C as a new userdirs.State() for the handful of things that are genuinely per-user (move sessions/ there from ~/.config — config directories should hold things a user might edit). doctor bundle learns both roots; doctor logs keeps its --worktree semantics by resolving through RuntimeRoot().

Windows checklist

Each item is a real failure mode seen in this repo's history or a documented platform difference; the convention is only worth having if these are encoded in the primitives, not remembered by reviewers.

  • Location. Keep config at %USERPROFILE%\.config\entire. It is non-idiomatic, but contexts.json and tokens.json are already there for every Windows user, and git-remote-entire reads the same path; moving it means a coordinated migration across two binaries for a cosmetic gain. New Data()/State() surfaces should use %LOCALAPPDATA%\entire as plugin_store.go already does. Document the asymmetry once in userdirs.
  • Permissions. 0600/0700 are no-ops; Chmod toggles read-only. EnsurePrivateDir already skips; ReadOwned's mode check must skip too. Privacy comes from the profile directory's inherited ACL, which is the norm for every other CLI (gh, aws, git).
  • Rename over an open file fails (ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION). Any concurrent reader — a second hook, Defender, an editor — makes WriteFileAtomic's rename fail. Retry with backoff (a few attempts over ~250 ms) inside the primitive; #455 was this in go-git's object store.
  • No directory fsync. Already best-effort; the branch's syncdir_windows.go whitelists ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION/ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED/ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. Keep that list in one place.
  • Locks leave .lock files behind. LockFileEx needs a real file; they already litter ~/.config/entire and .git/entire. Fine, but entire clean should know they are ours.
  • os.Root and junctions. A Root refuses to traverse an absolute symlink, and Windows junctions are reported as symlinks. A user whose ~/.config is a junction (Scoop users, OneDrive-redirected profiles) would get every user-tier read rejected if we anchored a Root above it. This is why the user tier resolves first, then opens, and never uses os.Root for its own files. The worktree tier keeps os.Root, where refusing junctions is the desired behaviour.
  • Reserved names and separators. os.Root rejects NUL, COM1… by itself; filepath.Join does not. paths.ValidateID is the one place that rejects them for plain joins, so an ID like con from a checkpoint can never create .entire/metadata/con.
  • Case folding. Repo keys and path exclusions fold on darwin/windows (repopolicy.caseInsensitivePaths); the repos map in the user file must be looked up with the same fold, or C:\Code\Cli and c:\code\cli become two entries.
  • MSYS/Git-Bash paths. Hooks run under Git for Windows' bash, which hands us /c/Users/...; paths.normalizeMSYSPath exists — every resolver that compares a hook-supplied path to a stored key must route through it.
  • Long paths. <git-common>\entire\worktree\<64-bit key>\metadata\<session>\tasks\<toolUseID>\agent-<id>.jsonl approaches MAX_PATH under a deep %USERPROFILE%. Go enables long-path awareness for \\?\-prefixed paths only when the manifest allows it; keep the key short (the branch already moved to 64-bit) and prefer opening through a Root handle, which sidesteps path-length limits for the relative part.
  • CI. #1843 added a Windows job; make safefile's tests the ones that exercise rename-under-open-handle, junction refusal in the worktree tier, and junction tolerance in the user tier, so the platform is tested where the rules live.

Decisions the team needs to make

  1. Does OPF's enabled/categories stay team-level? Proposal says yes — what gets redacted before it leaves a machine is a policy the repo owner sets; only how the binary is found is per-machine. The alternative (everything user-level) means a teammate without OPF installed silently pushes un-filtered content; the fail-closed pre-push already handles "enabled but missing binary", which is the right outcome.
  2. Per-block tolerant decoding of the user file vs. #2030's whole-file strictness. Needed before any key is added to the file, otherwise a nightly and a stable on one machine fight. Suggest folding it into the #2030 stack now, since that is where the loader lives.
  3. Runtime layout B for repo-enabled repos. One layout is a real simplification but a visible change (.entire/logs disappears from worktrees; docs and doctor hints move). Could ship behind the global-tier work or as its own follow-up.
  4. How hard to fence with lint. The os.UserHomeDir ban with an agent/** allow-list is cheap and catches the next stray resolver. Banning os.ReadFile in four packages is more work (many test helpers) but is what turns "please use the safe primitive" into something CI enforces, the way Worktree.Status is enforced today.
  5. Where ~/.config/entire/sessions/ (#1959) should live. If userdirs.State() is added, land #1959 on it rather than migrating later.
  6. Windows config location. Stay at ~\.config\entire (recommended) or migrate to %APPDATA% in lockstep across entire and git-remote-entire.
Suggested first PR

User-tier loader in settings (lifted from repopolicy/user_settings.go, per-block decode), safefile.ReadOwned/ReadConfined/WriteAtomic extracted from their current homes with no behaviour change, the os.UserHomeDir lint fence, and OPF command honored from the user file. Everything else layers on top, and that PR alone deletes the HEAD probe from the pre-push path.

Sources: cmd/entire/cli/settings/{settings,opf_command_trust}.go, internal/entireclient/userdirs, cmd/entire/cli/trail_context_cache.go, cmd/entire/cli/plugin_store.go, cmd/entire/cli/internal/flock, cmd/entire/cli/jsonutil/write.go; branch fix/global-takeover-migration: settings/repopolicy/*, settings/global.go, paths/invisible.go, docs/architecture/global-tracking.md; GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf, GHSA-2h46-9x5w-4wf7 (CVE-2026-57208); PRs #1365 #1449 #2030 #2154 #2156 #2163; go doc os.Root (go1.26.6).

entireio/cli · design investigation · 2026-08-28

Entire Filesystem Trust Tiers

A home for per-user configuration (OPF first), a place for preferences that today live in .git/entire/preferences.json, and one convention for where Entire reads and writes files so path-traversal and symlink fixes stop being whac-a-mole.

Investigated on main@8c77cdc + origin/main@a918e75 Branches read: feat/global-trust (#2030), fix/global-takeover-migration PRs read: #1365 #1449 #2154 #2156 #2163
Contents

  2. Two things you should know first
  3. Where Entire writes today
  4. What is already in flight
  5. The problems, precisely
  6. The convention: four trust tiers
  7. Primitives: what exists, what to add
  8. User settings file: schema and precedence

  10. Migration 2 — dissolving preferences.json
  11. Migration 3 — logs and tmp
  12. Windows checklist
  13. Decisions the team needs to make

Target posture, in one screen

Every file Entire touches falls into one of four tiers, and the tier — not the individual call site — decides how it is opened, who may set what in it, and whether its contents may ever name something to execute.

owner-trusted

User

~/.config/entire · ~/.cache/entire

The developer's own machine state. The only place exec-bearing settings (OPF command) are honored. Symlinks are legitimate here (dotfile managers). Private perms, strict decode where it matters.

machine-local, repo-scoped

Clone

<git-common-dir>/entire…

Shared by every worktree of one clone, never committed. Runtime and caches only: session state, redact cache, sync-remote capture, per-worktree runtime roots. No policy, no preferences.

repository-controlled

Worktree

<worktree>/.entire

Arrives with a clone. Configuration, never consent, never a command. Read through os.Root, symlinks refused (#2154/#2156), strict decode, IDs validated before joining paths.

hostile input

Remote

entire/checkpoints/v1 · API responses

Anyone with push access authored it (CVE-2026-57208). Every field that becomes a path is validated at the read boundary; every write lands through an os.Root anchored at the destination.

Main recommendation

Do not invent a new file. ~/.config/entire/settings.json already exists on your feat/global-trust stack (#2030) with a loader, a lock, an atomic symlink-following writer and 0600 perms. Grow that file: add a redaction.openai_privacy_filter block and a per-repo repos map, make it the only source for exec-bearing keys, and retire the git-index/HEAD "is this local file tracked?" probe from the hot path entirely. Then move the two kinds of content in preferences.json to where they belong — durable preferences to the user tier, the trails cache to ~/.cache.

Two things you should know first

Your main worktree is missing 1,355 tracked files

git status in the primary checkout reports 1,355 deletions — including go.mod, cmd/entire/cli/paths/, internal/entireclient/userdirs/ and the AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md symlink. There are no .icloud placeholders, and the last reflog entry is a clean pull: Fast-forward, so this is not a git operation you ran; the repo sits under iCloud Drive (Archive), which does not preserve symlinks and evicts aggressively. The .worktrees/global-settings-tier checkout shows the same symptom for AGENTS.md only. I did not touch the tree. Everything in this write-up was read from git objects (git show HEAD:…, branch refs) and from the intact .worktrees/ checkouts.

git restore . will bring the files back (the six real modifications are .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json, .entire/.gitignore, .entire/settings.json and two others), but the durable fix is to move the clone out of iCloud. Local main is also 127 commits behind origin/main, which matters here because #2154 and #2156 merged today.

I could not open the shared artifact

claude.ai/share/94e99223-… returns only the SPA shell to a fetch. If you paste the TL;DR text or re-share it as a claude.ai/code/artifact/… link I can reconcile this proposal against it. What follows is grounded in the code, the advisories and the in-flight PRs instead.

Where Entire writes today

Every on-disk surface, its resolver, and how it is written. The write idioms differ file to file — three lock/write styles, two permission conventions, three separate "where is the user's directory" resolvers — which is the first thing a convention should collapse.

What is already in flight

The two advisories and the PRs around them define the constraints any convention has to respect.

The advisories

  • GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf (high) — repository-controlled .entire/settings.json could select code to run: local_dev pointed hooks at the checkout, and OPF command became argv[0] at pre-push. Fixed by removing local_dev and honoring command only from an untracked settings.local.json (settings/opf_command_trust.go). The residual cost of that fix is a git-index read on every settings load and a HEAD read whenever the command is set locally — measured 8.3 ms → 2.5 ms per hook process, 39 ms → 11 ms on reftable.
  • CVE-2026-57208 (medium) — a SessionID from the remote entire/checkpoints/v1 branch was joined into a path during resume/rewind. Fixed in #1365/#1449 by validating IDs at the read boundary and writing session state through os.Root (session/state.go, state.go).

Merged today

  • #2154 — paths.ValidateEntireDirAt: .entire must be a real directory (Lstat, so a symlink to a good directory is still refused); root PersistentPreRunE guards every command, with an audited exemption list.
  • #2156 — extends the guard one level down (no symlinks/FIFOs among .entire's direct children, fs.ModeIrregular masked for OneDrive placeholders) and makes readConfined refuse symlinked settings files with a post-open SameFile re-check.

Open

  • #2163 (pjbgf) — userdirs.EnsurePrivateDir: create at 0700 and strip group/other bits from an existing dir; skipped on Windows.
  • #2030 (yours, feat/global-trust; freshest head fix/global-takeover-migration, 161 commits ahead) — introduces ~/.config/entire/settings.json with a global block, repopolicy.LoadUserSettings/ModifyUserSettings, userdirs.ResolveConfig() (error-returning, never CWD-relative), jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks with cycle detection, a hook-boundary policy snapshot on ctx, and RepoPolicy.RuntimeRoot() routing runtime data to <git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/ for globally tracked repos. Your own machine already has {"global":{"enabled":true}} in that file.
  • #1959 (session binding) — writes ~/.config/entire/sessions/<id>.json via userdirs.Config(). That is state, not config, and it is the first thing that would move under a state/data directory if one existed.
Compatibility hazard already latent in #2030

LoadUserSettings strict-decodes the whole file and any unknown key turns the global tier off machine-wide (by design, fail closed). The moment a newer binary adds redaction or repos to that file, every older entire on the same machine — a pinned Scoop install, a CI image, the git-remote-entire helper if it ever reads it — stops tracking. Extending the file requires a decode rule that is strict per block (unknown top-level keys tolerated with a warning; unknown keys inside a security-bearing block still fail that block closed). See schema.

The problems, precisely

1. settings.local.json is per worktree, and it is where the sensitive knobs live

Linked worktrees are the norm in this repo (fifteen under .worktrees/). Every one needs its own settings.local.json to carry the OPF command, the checkpoint_remote, the investigate config. Nothing propagates. And because the file sits inside content the repository controls, the loader has to prove on every load that the file is not tracked — that is the index probe, and for OPF the HEAD probe. The security work is paying for a location choice.

2. preferences.json mixes two lifetimes

Review profiles are a developer's durable preference for a repo. The trails enablement cache is a one-hour network answer keyed by repo_key + api_base + auth_key — all three are properties of the user's identity and the remote, not of the clone. Putting them in one file means every SessionStart refresh rewrites the review prefs, the cache is duplicated per clone of the same repo, and the writer has to run git rev-parse --git-common-dir under a 3 s deadline (the comment in trail_context_cache.go about answering at 2.9 s and then failing to store is exactly this). It is also written 0644 in a 0750 directory, lenient-decoded, with no owner semantics at all.

3. Three "user directory" resolvers, three write idioms

userdirs (config/cache), plugin_store.go (data, Windows-aware), and 16 bare os.UserHomeDir() calls. Writers use gofrs/flock, internal/flock, or no lock; dirs are 0700, 0750 or 0755 depending on which code path ran first. #2163 exists precisely because of that last point.

4. The safety story is per call site

readConfined is right but lives privately in settings; osroot (on the global branches) is a thin, unwrapped helper; state.go, clean.go and session/state.go each open their own os.Root. Each fix is correct and none is reusable, so the next path-bearing field will be joined with filepath.Join again.

5. Windows gets the non-idiomatic location and the least-tested primitives

Config resolves to %USERPROFILE%\.config\entire, permissions are synthetic, os.Rename onto an open file fails with a sharing violation, directory fsync is unsupported, and os.Root treats junctions as symlinks (so an os.Root anchored above a junctioned ~/.config refuses to read through it). Twenty-plus Windows issues in the tracker (#455 object-rename Access Denied, #886, #1424, #1398, #1707…) say the platform needs the convention to be explicit, not implied.

The convention: four trust tiers

One table the whole team can point at in review. "Owner" is who can put bytes in the file without local access to the developer's machine; every other column follows from it.

TierOwnerMay carryMust never carryRead disciplineWrite disciplineSymlinks

Unix: refuse a file writable by group/other (matches OpenSSH's stance on ~/.ssh/config)EnsurePrivateDir (0700) → flock on <file>.lock → temp in same dir → fsync → rename through the resolved target → best-effort dir sync. Files 0600.Followed (dotfile managers)

No consent bits.ValidateEntireDirAt (#2154/#2156) then readConfined; strict decode; the "is it tracked?" probe becomes unnecessary once nothing exec-bearing is read hereRuntime writes only (metadata/logs/tmp), always via os.Root at .entireRefused (merged today)

Why the tiers are shaped this way

  • Exec-bearing keys live in one tier, so trust needs one check. Today enforceOPFCommandTrust proves a repo file is not tracked (index + HEAD) because the file sits in the repo. A file under ~/.config needs no such proof — the repository cannot reach it. The whole classifyLocalSettingsDeep path and its memoization go away.
  • Symlink policy flips at the boundary. #2156 is right to refuse symlinks inside .entire, because a repository put them there. The same rule applied to ~/.config/entire would break every stow/chezmoi user; the branch's WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks already encodes the opposite policy. Making "symlinks followed?" a property of the tier, not of the helper, keeps both correct.
  • Clone tier stops holding preferences. A developer who rm -rfs a clone and re-clones expects their review setup to survive; a developer with two clones of the same repo expects one setting. Both point at the user tier keyed by repo, which the global tier already has a normalized key for (host/owner/repo, repopolicy.NormalizeOrigin).
  • Runtime consolidates under one root per clone. #2030 already introduces <git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/ for global mode. Adopting it for repo-enabled mode too gives one layout, one os.Root anchor, and a byte-clean git status everywhere — but it is a behaviour change (`doctor bundle`, log tailing docs) and is listed as a decision, not assumed.

Primitives: what exists, what to add

Most of the pieces already exist somewhere on main or the global stack. The proposal is to gather them into two packages with a lint fence around them, so a reviewer flags a raw os.ReadFile the same way they flag a raw git.PlainOpen today.

Go's os.Root: what it does and does not give you (Go 1.26.6 doc)

Confines every method to the directory; follows symlinks but refuses ones that escape or are absolute; on Windows also rejects reserved device names and treats junctions as symlinks. It does not stop bind mounts or /proc, and Chmod/Chown/Chtimes race against a file-to-symlink swap on Unix — so set perms on the open file (f.Chmod, as the branch's writer now does), never by path. Every helper in safefile should carry that list in its doc comment so call sites stop re-deriving it.

User settings file: schema and precedence

One file, ~/.config/entire/settings.json, hand-editable, documented as stable. Blocks are independent so a block can be strict without the file being brittle.

{
  // exists today on feat/global-trust — unchanged
  "global": {
    "enabled": true,
    "exclude_paths": ["~/scratch/**"],
    "trust_all": false,
    "trusted_origins": ["github.com/entireio/cli"]
  },

  // NEW — how OPF runs on THIS machine. "enabled"/"categories" stay in the
  // team's .entire/settings.json (what to redact is policy; how to run it is local).
  "redaction": {
    "openai_privacy_filter": {
      "command": "/opt/homebrew/bin/opf",
      "timeout_seconds": 120,
      "prompt_default": "ask"
    }
  },

  // NEW — machine-wide developer defaults (were per-worktree in settings.local.json)
  "review_profiles": { "quick": { "agent": "claude-code", "skills": ["/review"] } },
  "review_default_profile": "quick",
  "investigate": { "agents": ["claude-code", "codex"], "max_turns": 2 },
  "summary_generation": { "provider": "claude-code" },

  // NEW — per-repository overrides, keyed like trusted_origins
  "repos": {
    "github.com/entireio/cli": {
      "review_default_profile": "pr-toolkit",
      "review_profiles": { "pr-toolkit": { "agent": "claude-code", "skills": ["/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr"] } },
      "strategy_options": { "checkpoint_remote": { "provider": "github", "repo": "peyton-alt/cli-checkpoints" } }
    },
    // no-origin repos key by canonical path, same rule as trusted_paths
    "/Users/me/code/notes": { "review_default_profile": "quick" }
  }
}

Decode rule

  • Top level: tolerant. Unknown top-level keys are kept as json.RawMessage, round-tripped on write, and reported once by entire doctor ("key foo is not understood by this version"). This is what lets a 0.11 binary and a 0.12 binary share a machine.
  • Inside global and redaction: strict, fail that block closed — exactly #2030's current behaviour, scoped to the blocks where an unrecognized key could mean an unrecognized exclusion or an unrecognized command option.
  • Inside preferences blocks (review_*, investigate, summary_generation, repos.*): strict on the known struct, but a failure drops the block with a warning rather than the file. Losing a review preference must never disable tracking.

Precedence (lowest → highest)

  1. <worktree>/.entire/settings.json — team
  2. User file, top-level blocks — me, every repo
  3. User file, repos["<key>"] — me, this repo, every worktree of every clone
  4. <worktree>/.entire/settings.local.json — me, this worktree only. Kept for what is genuinely per-worktree (enabled for enable --local, an experiment in one checkout). Exec-bearing keys are no longer read from here.

Consent stays where #2030 put it: global.trust_* is the only egress switch, a committed enabled: false still vetoes, and nothing in the repository can open the sync path. The per-repo checkpoint_remote moving to the user tier actually strengthens CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly: "the developer chose this remote" becomes a fact about which file it came from, with no tracked-file probe needed.

Migration 1 — OPF out of the worktree

Smallest useful slice; ships independently of #2030 landing, because the user file's loader can be lifted into settings on its own.

  1. Loader. settings.Load reads the user file after the project file and before the local file. enforceOPFCommandTrust gains a first case: command came from the user file → accept, no probe. The existing local-file path stays for one release.
  2. Deprecate the local path. When command is found in settings.local.json, honor it (probe and all) but print once per day: "OPF command is read from ~/.config/entire/settings.json from v0.13; run entire configure --opf-command <path> to move it." entire doctor lists the file and the fix.
  3. Remove. Next minor: drop the local-file case, delete classifyLocalSettingsDeep and the HEAD probe. The shallow index probe remains only until the local layer stops being a security input at all (it still gates CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly today; that goes with Migration 2).
  4. Windows. The command is exec'd directly (never via cmd.exe, per CLAUDE.md); accept opf.exe, paths with spaces, and %LOCALAPPDATA%-style values only if expanded by the user's shell — do not expand env vars in the setting. Reject a relative command (it would resolve against the repo CWD) unless it is a bare name resolved on PATH with exec.ErrDot protection, as today.
  5. Docs. docs/security-and-privacy.md "Why command is local-only" becomes "Why command is user-only" — the argument gets shorter, which is the point.

What this buys: one OPF setting per machine instead of per worktree; the pre-push trust gate no longer reads the git index or HEAD; the exec boundary is expressible in one sentence ("Entire only executes what ~/.config/entire names").

Migration 2 — dissolving preferences.json

The file has three kinds of content; each has a better home. Once they move, ClonePreferences and its loader delete outright.

ContentLifetimeMove toWhy
review_profiles, review_default_profile, legacy review, review_fix_agentDurable preferenceuser repos["<key>"].review_*, falling back to top-level review_*Survives re-clone; shared across clones and worktrees; the picker writes one place. The one-shot migration prompt in review/picker.go already knows how to move keys between files — point it at the new destination.
review_migration_dismissedDurable flaguser top-levelA user's answer, not a clone's.
trails_enabled*, trails_agent_help_*1 h cache / 5 min backoffuser ~/.cache/entire/repos/<key>/trails.jsonAlready keyed by repo_key + api_base + auth_key — user-scoped by construction. No git rev-parse on the write path; one answer per repo per machine; safe to delete; entire clean can sweep it.
GlobalSetupCompleted (feat/global-writer)Stampclone <git-common>/entire/…It records that this clone was set up; #2030's later heads already replaced it with the derived primary-ref-ready stamp in the runtime root.

Order of work

  1. Trails cache first — it is a cache, so the migration is "start writing the new location, stop reading the old". Zero user-visible change.
  2. Review prefs second, behind the existing picker migration prompt: on first entire review with a populated preferences.json, copy into repos["<key>"] and rename the old file to preferences.json.migrated. Read the old file as a fallback for one release.
  3. Delete ClonePreferences, applyClonePreferences, and the preferencesFileAbs parameter of loadMergedSettings. settings.Load stops shelling out to git rev-parse --git-common-dir on every call (it does today, via clonePreferencesPathForWorktreeRoot, purely to find this file).

Repo key for repos without an origin

Reuse #2030's TrustIdentity rule exactly: origin present and every fetch/push URL normalizes → keyed by host/owner/repo; otherwise keyed by canonical worktree path. One rule, already documented, already tested for Windows drive letters and case folding.

Migration 3 — logs and tmp

Three candidate homes for .entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}; the choice is about layout, not trust, since all three are Entire-owned and gitignored or outside the tree.

A · Keep <worktree>/.entire/… for repo-enabled repos (status quo)

No migration; doctor bundle and docs unchanged. Cost: two layouts to reason about once #2030 lands (global repos use B), and the runtime dir sits inside a tree the repository controls, so it needs the #2154/#2156 guard forever.

B · <git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/… for every active repo ← recommended

#2030 already builds this for global mode; adopting it for local mode gives one layout, one os.Root anchor, byte-clean git status in every repo, and takes runtime data out of the repository-controlled tier. Cost: a one-time move of existing logs (or just start fresh — full.jsonl is regenerated per Stop), and the temp file for an atomic write must be on the same filesystem as its destination (it will be — same .git).

C · ~/.local/state/entire/repos/<key>/… (XDG state; %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows)

Right for logs that are not about one repo (login, version check, the future session-binding records currently in ~/.config/entire/sessions/). Wrong for metadata/tmp: hooks would write across filesystems, and two clones of one repo would collide on the key.

So: B for repo runtime, C as a new userdirs.State() for the handful of things that are genuinely per-user (move sessions/ there from ~/.config — config directories should hold things a user might edit). doctor bundle learns both roots; doctor logs keeps its --worktree semantics by resolving through RuntimeRoot().

Windows checklist

Each item is a real failure mode seen in this repo's history or a documented platform difference; the convention is only worth having if these are encoded in the primitives, not remembered by reviewers.

  • Location. Keep config at %USERPROFILE%\.config\entire. It is non-idiomatic, but contexts.json and tokens.json are already there for every Windows user, and git-remote-entire reads the same path; moving it means a coordinated migration across two binaries for a cosmetic gain. New Data()/State() surfaces should use %LOCALAPPDATA%\entire as plugin_store.go already does. Document the asymmetry once in userdirs.
  • Permissions. 0600/0700 are no-ops; Chmod toggles read-only. EnsurePrivateDir already skips; ReadOwned's mode check must skip too. Privacy comes from the profile directory's inherited ACL, which is the norm for every other CLI (gh, aws, git).
  • Rename over an open file fails (ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION). Any concurrent reader — a second hook, Defender, an editor — makes WriteFileAtomic's rename fail. Retry with backoff (a few attempts over ~250 ms) inside the primitive; #455 was this in go-git's object store.
  • No directory fsync. Already best-effort; the branch's syncdir_windows.go whitelists ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION/ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED/ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. Keep that list in one place.
  • Locks leave .lock files behind. LockFileEx needs a real file; they already litter ~/.config/entire and .git/entire. Fine, but entire clean should know they are ours.
  • os.Root and junctions. A Root refuses to traverse an absolute symlink, and Windows junctions are reported as symlinks. A user whose ~/.config is a junction (Scoop users, OneDrive-redirected profiles) would get every user-tier read rejected if we anchored a Root above it. This is why the user tier resolves first, then opens, and never uses os.Root for its own files. The worktree tier keeps os.Root, where refusing junctions is the desired behaviour.
  • Reserved names and separators. os.Root rejects NUL, COM1… by itself; filepath.Join does not. paths.ValidateID is the one place that rejects them for plain joins, so an ID like con from a checkpoint can never create .entire/metadata/con.
  • Case folding. Repo keys and path exclusions fold on darwin/windows (repopolicy.caseInsensitivePaths); the repos map in the user file must be looked up with the same fold, or C:\Code\Cli and c:\code\cli become two entries.
  • MSYS/Git-Bash paths. Hooks run under Git for Windows' bash, which hands us /c/Users/...; paths.normalizeMSYSPath exists — every resolver that compares a hook-supplied path to a stored key must route through it.
  • Long paths. <git-common>\entire\worktree\<64-bit key>\metadata\<session>\tasks\<toolUseID>\agent-<id>.jsonl approaches MAX_PATH under a deep %USERPROFILE%. Go enables long-path awareness for \\?\-prefixed paths only when the manifest allows it; keep the key short (the branch already moved to 64-bit) and prefer opening through a Root handle, which sidesteps path-length limits for the relative part.
  • CI. #1843 added a Windows job; make safefile's tests the ones that exercise rename-under-open-handle, junction refusal in the worktree tier, and junction tolerance in the user tier, so the platform is tested where the rules live.

Decisions the team needs to make

  1. Does OPF's enabled/categories stay team-level? Proposal says yes — what gets redacted before it leaves a machine is a policy the repo owner sets; only how the binary is found is per-machine. The alternative (everything user-level) means a teammate without OPF installed silently pushes un-filtered content; the fail-closed pre-push already handles "enabled but missing binary", which is the right outcome.
  2. Per-block tolerant decoding of the user file vs. #2030's whole-file strictness. Needed before any key is added to the file, otherwise a nightly and a stable on one machine fight. Suggest folding it into the #2030 stack now, since that is where the loader lives.
  3. Runtime layout B for repo-enabled repos. One layout is a real simplification but a visible change (.entire/logs disappears from worktrees; docs and doctor hints move). Could ship behind the global-tier work or as its own follow-up.
  4. How hard to fence with lint. The os.UserHomeDir ban with an agent/** allow-list is cheap and catches the next stray resolver. Banning os.ReadFile in four packages is more work (many test helpers) but is what turns "please use the safe primitive" into something CI enforces, the way Worktree.Status is enforced today.
  5. Where ~/.config/entire/sessions/ (#1959) should live. If userdirs.State() is added, land #1959 on it rather than migrating later.
  6. Windows config location. Stay at ~\.config\entire (recommended) or migrate to %APPDATA% in lockstep across entire and git-remote-entire.
Suggested first PR

User-tier loader in settings (lifted from repopolicy/user_settings.go, per-block decode), safefile.ReadOwned/ReadConfined/WriteAtomic extracted from their current homes with no behaviour change, the os.UserHomeDir lint fence, and OPF command honored from the user file. Everything else layers on top, and that PR alone deletes the HEAD probe from the pre-push path.

Sources: cmd/entire/cli/settings/{settings,opf_command_trust}.go, internal/entireclient/userdirs, cmd/entire/cli/trail_context_cache.go, cmd/entire/cli/plugin_store.go, cmd/entire/cli/internal/flock, cmd/entire/cli/jsonutil/write.go; branch fix/global-takeover-migration: settings/repopolicy/*, settings/global.go, paths/invisible.go, docs/architecture/global-tracking.md; GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf, GHSA-2h46-9x5w-4wf7 (CVE-2026-57208); PRs #1365 #1449 #2030 #2154 #2156 #2163; go doc os.Root (go1.26.6).

<git-common>/entire-sessions/ · entire-session-locks · entire-redact-cache · entire-search · entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json    clone    Session state, locks, incremental redaction prefixes, search cache, captured sync-remote election    Each has its own path constant; session state uses os.Root (#1365)    Five sibling top-level names in .git/; on the global branch runtime moves under .git/entire/worktree/<key>/.
<worktree>/.entire/settings.json    worktree    Team configuration, committed    readConfined: os.Root at parent + Lstat + post-open re-check (#2156), strict decode    GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf: this file once selected code to execute (local_dev, OPF command).
<worktree>/.entire/settings.local.json    worktree    enable --local, OPF command, checkpoint_remote, investigate config, review --local profiles, summary provider    Same reader, plus classifyLocalSettings (git index probe) on every settings.Load; the OPF command adds a HEAD probe    Per worktree, not per clone. Gitignored, but .gitignore does not apply to an already-tracked path, hence the probe.
<worktree>/.entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}    worktree    Runtime: shadow-tree staging, entire.log, hook scratch    paths.AbsPath; state.go/clean.go use os.Root for tmp    Gitignored. The global tier relocates these to <git-common>/entire/worktree/<hash>/ for globally tracked repos.
Agent home dirs (~/.claude, ~/.gemini, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, …)    user    Transcripts we read; hooks we install    16 direct os.UserHomeDir() calls across agent/*, plus setup.go (shell rc), utils.go, global_warn.go    Legitimately outside userdirs, but they should be the allow-list for a lint rule, not the norm.
What is already in flight
The two advisories and the PRs around them define the constraints any convention has to respect.

The advisories
GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf (high) — repository-controlled .entire/settings.json could select code to run: local_dev pointed hooks at the checkout, and OPF command became argv[0] at pre-push. Fixed by removing local_dev and honoring command only from an untracked settings.local.json (settings/opf_command_trust.go). The residual cost of that fix is a git-index read on every settings load and a HEAD read whenever the command is set locally — measured 8.3 ms → 2.5 ms per hook process, 39 ms → 11 ms on reftable.
CVE-2026-57208 (medium) — a SessionID from the remote entire/checkpoints/v1 branch was joined into a path during resume/rewind. Fixed in #1365/#1449 by validating IDs at the read boundary and writing session state through os.Root (session/state.go, state.go).
Merged today
#2154 — paths.ValidateEntireDirAt: .entire must be a real directory (Lstat, so a symlink to a good directory is still refused); root PersistentPreRunE guards every command, with an audited exemption list.
#2156 — extends the guard one level down (no symlinks/FIFOs among .entire's direct children, fs.ModeIrregular masked for OneDrive placeholders) and makes readConfined refuse symlinked settings files with a post-open SameFile re-check.
Open
#2163 (pjbgf) — userdirs.EnsurePrivateDir: create at 0700 and strip group/other bits from an existing dir; skipped on Windows.
#2030 (yours, feat/global-trust; freshest head fix/global-takeover-migration, 161 commits ahead) — introduces ~/.config/entire/settings.json with a global block, repopolicy.LoadUserSettings/ModifyUserSettings, userdirs.ResolveConfig() (error-returning, never CWD-relative), jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks with cycle detection, a hook-boundary policy snapshot on ctx, and RepoPolicy.RuntimeRoot() routing runtime data to <git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/ for globally tracked repos. Your own machine already has {"global":{"enabled":true}} in that file.
#1959 (session binding) — writes ~/.config/entire/sessions/<id>.json via userdirs.Config(). That is state, not config, and it is the first thing that would move under a state/data directory if one existed.
Compatibility hazard already latent in #2030
LoadUserSettings strict-decodes the whole file and any unknown key turns the global tier off machine-wide (by design, fail closed). The moment a newer binary adds redaction or repos to that file, every older entire on the same machine — a pinned Scoop install, a CI image, the git-remote-entire helper if it ever reads it — stops tracking. Extending the file requires a decode rule that is strict per block (unknown top-level keys tolerated with a warning; unknown keys inside a security-bearing block still fail that block closed). See schema.

The problems, precisely
1. settings.local.json is per worktree, and it is where the sensitive knobs live
Linked worktrees are the norm in this repo (fifteen under .worktrees/). Every one needs its own settings.local.json to carry the OPF command, the checkpoint_remote, the investigate config. Nothing propagates. And because the file sits inside content the repository controls, the loader has to prove on every load that the file is not tracked — that is the index probe, and for OPF the HEAD probe. The security work is paying for a location choice.

2. preferences.json mixes two lifetimes
Review profiles are a developer's durable preference for a repo. The trails enablement cache is a one-hour network answer keyed by repo_key + api_base + auth_key — all three are properties of the user's identity and the remote, not of the clone. Putting them in one file means every SessionStart refresh rewrites the review prefs, the cache is duplicated per clone of the same repo, and the writer has to run git rev-parse --git-common-dir under a 3 s deadline (the comment in trail_context_cache.go about answering at 2.9 s and then failing to store is exactly this). It is also written 0644 in a 0750 directory, lenient-decoded, with no owner semantics at all.

3. Three "user directory" resolvers, three write idioms
userdirs (config/cache), plugin_store.go (data, Windows-aware), and 16 bare os.UserHomeDir() calls. Writers use gofrs/flock, internal/flock, or no lock; dirs are 0700, 0750 or 0755 depending on which code path ran first. #2163 exists precisely because of that last point.

4. The safety story is per call site
readConfined is right but lives privately in settings; osroot (on the global branches) is a thin, unwrapped helper; state.go, clean.go and session/state.go each open their own os.Root. Each fix is correct and none is reusable, so the next path-bearing field will be joined with filepath.Join again.

5. Windows gets the non-idiomatic location and the least-tested primitives
Config resolves to %USERPROFILE%\.config\entire, permissions are synthetic, os.Rename onto an open file fails with a sharing violation, directory fsync is unsupported, and os.Root treats junctions as symlinks (so an os.Root anchored above a junctioned ~/.config refuses to read through it). Twenty-plus Windows issues in the tracker (#455 object-rename Access Denied, #886, #1424, #1398, #1707…) say the platform needs the convention to be explicit, not implied.

The convention: four trust tiers
One table the whole team can point at in review. "Owner" is who can put bytes in the file without local access to the developer's machine; every other column follows from it.

Tier    Owner    May carry    Must never carry    Read discipline    Write discipline    Symlinks
user    The developer    Identity, consent (trust_*), exec-bearing settings (command), per-repo preferences, machine caches, cross-repo state    Anything derived from repository or remote content without validation    Resolve symlinks, then open; strict-per-block decode; a parse error fails that block closed. Unix: refuse a file writable by group/other (matches OpenSSH's stance on ~/.ssh/config)    EnsurePrivateDir (0700) → flock on <file>.lock → temp in same dir → fsync → rename through the resolved target → best-effort dir sync. Files 0600.    Followed (dotfile managers)
clone    The developer, indirectly the repository (hooks path, .git contents arrive with the clone only for bare/shared setups)    Runtime and caches that are inherently per clone: session state, locks, redact prefixes, sync-remote capture, per-worktree runtime roots (metadata/logs/tmp in global mode)    Policy records, preferences, anything a user would want to survive rm -rf of the clone    Paths built only from validated IDs; open through an os.Root anchored at <git-common>/entire    Same atomic writer; one lock helper; dir 0700    Not followed
worktree    Anyone who can push to the repository    Team configuration and per-worktree developer overrides: enabled, redaction categories/engines, review profiles, strategy options    Any string that becomes argv[0], an env value, a hook path, or a URL Entire will authenticate to. No consent bits.    ValidateEntireDirAt (#2154/#2156) then readConfined; strict decode; the "is it tracked?" probe becomes unnecessary once nothing exec-bearing is read here    Runtime writes only (metadata/logs/tmp), always via os.Root at .entire    Refused (merged today)
remote    Anyone with push access to the checkpoint branch, or the API    Data    Paths. A field is an identifier until paths.ValidateID says otherwise    Validate every ID at the decode boundary; errors.Is the sentinel, never string-match    Restore writes go through root.OpenFile/root.Rename on a Root at the destination; never os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(...))    Refused
Why the tiers are shaped this way
Exec-bearing keys live in one tier, so trust needs one check. Today enforceOPFCommandTrust proves a repo file is not tracked (index + HEAD) because the file sits in the repo. A file under ~/.config needs no such proof — the repository cannot reach it. The whole classifyLocalSettingsDeep path and its memoization go away.
Symlink policy flips at the boundary. #2156 is right to refuse symlinks inside .entire, because a repository put them there. The same rule applied to ~/.config/entire would break every stow/chezmoi user; the branch's WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks already encodes the opposite policy. Making "symlinks followed?" a property of the tier, not of the helper, keeps both correct.
Clone tier stops holding preferences. A developer who rm -rfs a clone and re-clones expects their review setup to survive; a developer with two clones of the same repo expects one setting. Both point at the user tier keyed by repo, which the global tier already has a normalized key for (host/owner/repo, repopolicy.NormalizeOrigin).
Runtime consolidates under one root per clone. #2030 already introduces <git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/ for global mode. Adopting it for repo-enabled mode too gives one layout, one os.Root anchor, and a byte-clean git status everywhere — but it is a behaviour change (`doctor bundle`, log tailing docs) and is listed as a decision, not assumed.
Primitives: what exists, what to add
Most of the pieces already exist somewhere on main or the global stack. The proposal is to gather them into two packages with a lint fence around them, so a reviewer flags a raw os.ReadFile the same way they flag a raw git.PlainOpen today.

Need    Exists today    Proposed home    Change
Resolve user config / cache / data / state    userdirs.Config/Cache (main), ResolveConfig/ResolveCache (branch), EnsurePrivateDir (#2163), pluginParentDir (plugin_store.go)    internal/entireclient/userdirs    Add Data()/State() (XDG on Unix, %LOCALAPPDATA%\entire on Windows); fold pluginParentDir in; reject a relative ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR like ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR already does; extend testdirs for the new surfaces
Read an owner-trusted file    os.ReadFile in LoadUserSettings, contexts.readNoLock    internal/safefile (new)    ReadOwned(path): EvalSymlinks → open → fstat → (Unix) refuse if not owned by euid or writable by group/other → read. Windows: skip the mode check (ACLs inherit from the profile dir).
Read a repository-controlled file    settings.readConfined + validateOpenedFile (origin/main), osroot.ReadFile (branch)    internal/safefile    Export as ReadConfined(dir, base); keep the Lstat → Open → re-Lstat/SameFile shape; return paths.SymlinkedEntryError so callers keep their errors.Is
Atomic write    jsonutil.WriteFileAtomic (main), WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks + SyncDir per-OS (branch)    internal/safefile    Move out of jsonutil (it is not JSON-specific); add WriteConfined(root *os.Root, base, data, perm) using root.OpenFile + root.Rename; on Windows retry the rename on ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION/ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED with a short backoff (#455 is this failure)
Locked read-modify-write    gofrs/flock (contexts.go), internal/flock (prefs, user settings, sessions)    internal/flock    One Modify(ctx, path, perm, func([]byte) ([]byte, error)) that owns lock + read + write; drop the gofrs dependency
Validate an identifier before it becomes a path    Session-ID validation from #1365 (session/state.go), droid link-ID check (#1735 follow-ups), paths.IsRelativeTraversal    paths    ValidateID(kind, s): single-component, no separators, no ./.., printable, length-capped, and on Windows no reserved device names (os.Root rejects them, but a plain filepath.Join path does not)
Guard a directory Entire owns inside untrusted space    paths.ValidateEntireDirAt / RequireEntireDir (#2154/#2156)    paths    Reuse for <git-common>/entire (same shape: must be a real dir, no symlinked children)
Lint fence    forbidigo already bans os.Getwd, go-git Reset/Checkout/Worktree.Status    .golangci.yaml    Ban os.UserHomeDir/os.UserConfigDir/os.UserCacheDir outside userdirs and an agent/** allow-list; ban os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile/os.Open inside settings, checkpoint, session, strategy so those packages go through safefile; ban os.OpenRoot outside safefile/paths so there is one place that knows the platform caveats
Go's os.Root: what it does and does not give you (Go 1.26.6 doc)
Confines every method to the directory; follows symlinks but refuses ones that escape or are absolute; on Windows also rejects reserved device names and treats junctions as symlinks. It does not stop bind mounts or /proc, and Chmod/Chown/Chtimes race against a file-to-symlink swap on Unix — so set perms on the open file (f.Chmod, as the branch's writer now does), never by path. Every helper in safefile should carry that list in its doc comment so call sites stop re-deriving it.

User settings file: schema and precedence
One file, ~/.config/entire/settings.json, hand-editable, documented as stable. Blocks are independent so a block can be strict without the file being brittle.

{
  // exists today on feat/global-trust — unchanged
  "global": {
    "enabled": true,
    "exclude_paths": ["~/scratch/**"],
    "trust_all": false,
    "trusted_origins": ["github.com/entireio/cli"]
  },

  // NEW — how OPF runs on THIS machine. "enabled"/"categories" stay in the
  // team's .entire/settings.json (what to redact is policy; how to run it is local).
  "redaction": {
    "openai_privacy_filter": {
      "command": "/opt/homebrew/bin/opf",
      "timeout_seconds": 120,
      "prompt_default": "ask"
    }
  },

  // NEW — machine-wide developer defaults (were per-worktree in settings.local.json)
  "review_profiles": { "quick": { "agent": "claude-code", "skills": ["/review"] } },
  "review_default_profile": "quick",
  "investigate": { "agents": ["claude-code", "codex"], "max_turns": 2 },
  "summary_generation": { "provider": "claude-code" },

  // NEW — per-repository overrides, keyed like trusted_origins
  "repos": {
    "github.com/entireio/cli": {
      "review_default_profile": "pr-toolkit",
      "review_profiles": { "pr-toolkit": { "agent": "claude-code", "skills": ["/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr"] } },
      "strategy_options": { "checkpoint_remote": { "provider": "github", "repo": "peyton-alt/cli-checkpoints" } }
    },
    // no-origin repos key by canonical path, same rule as trusted_paths
    "/Users/me/code/notes": { "review_default_profile": "quick" }
  }
}
Decode rule
Top level: tolerant. Unknown top-level keys are kept as json.RawMessage, round-tripped on write, and reported once by entire doctor ("key foo is not understood by this version"). This is what lets a 0.11 binary and a 0.12 binary share a machine.
Inside global and redaction: strict, fail that block closed — exactly #2030's current behaviour, scoped to the blocks where an unrecognized key could mean an unrecognized exclusion or an unrecognized command option.
Inside preferences blocks (review_*, investigate, summary_generation, repos.*): strict on the known struct, but a failure drops the block with a warning rather than the file. Losing a review preference must never disable tracking.
Precedence (lowest → highest)
<worktree>/.entire/settings.json — team
User file, top-level blocks — me, every repo
User file, repos["<key>"] — me, this repo, every worktree of every clone
<worktree>/.entire/settings.local.json — me, this worktree only. Kept for what is genuinely per-worktree (enabled for enable --local, an experiment in one checkout). Exec-bearing keys are no longer read from here.
Consent stays where #2030 put it: global.trust_* is the only egress switch, a committed enabled: false still vetoes, and nothing in the repository can open the sync path. The per-repo checkpoint_remote moving to the user tier actually strengthens CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly: "the developer chose this remote" becomes a fact about which file it came from, with no tracked-file probe needed.

Migration 1 — OPF out of the worktree
Smallest useful slice; ships independently of #2030 landing, because the user file's loader can be lifted into settings on its own.

Loader. settings.Load reads the user file after the project file and before the local file. enforceOPFCommandTrust gains a first case: command came from the user file → accept, no probe. The existing local-file path stays for one release.
Deprecate the local path. When command is found in settings.local.json, honor it (probe and all) but print once per day: "OPF command is read from ~/.config/entire/settings.json from v0.13; run entire configure --opf-command <path> to move it." entire doctor lists the file and the fix.
Remove. Next minor: drop the local-file case, delete classifyLocalSettingsDeep and the HEAD probe. The shallow index probe remains only until the local layer stops being a security input at all (it still gates CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly today; that goes with Migration 2).
Windows. The command is exec'd directly (never via cmd.exe, per CLAUDE.md); accept opf.exe, paths with spaces, and %LOCALAPPDATA%-style values only if expanded by the user's shell — do not expand env vars in the setting. Reject a relative command (it would resolve against the repo CWD) unless it is a bare name resolved on PATH with exec.ErrDot protection, as today.
Docs. docs/security-and-privacy.md "Why command is local-only" becomes "Why command is user-only" — the argument gets shorter, which is the point.
What this buys: one OPF setting per machine instead of per worktree; the pre-push trust gate no longer reads the git index or HEAD; the exec boundary is expressible in one sentence ("Entire only executes what ~/.config/entire names").

Migration 2 — dissolving preferences.json
The file has three kinds of content; each has a better home. Once they move, ClonePreferences and its loader delete outright.

Content    Lifetime    Move to    Why
review_profiles, review_default_profile, legacy review, review_fix_agent    Durable preference    user repos["<key>"].review_*, falling back to top-level review_*    Survives re-clone; shared across clones and worktrees; the picker writes one place. The one-shot migration prompt in review/picker.go already knows how to move keys between files — point it at the new destination.
review_migration_dismissed    Durable flag    user top-level    A user's answer, not a clone's.
trails_enabled*, trails_agent_help_*    1 h cache / 5 min backoff    user ~/.cache/entire/repos/<key>/trails.json    Already keyed by repo_key + api_base + auth_key — user-scoped by construction. No git rev-parse on the write path; one answer per repo per machine; safe to delete; entire clean can sweep it.
GlobalSetupCompleted (feat/global-writer)    Stamp    clone <git-common>/entire/…    It records that this clone was set up; #2030's later heads already replaced it with the derived primary-ref-ready stamp in the runtime root.
Order of work
Trails cache first — it is a cache, so the migration is "start writing the new location, stop reading the old". Zero user-visible change.
Review prefs second, behind the existing picker migration prompt: on first entire review with a populated preferences.json, copy into repos["<key>"] and rename the old file to preferences.json.migrated. Read the old file as a fallback for one release.
Delete ClonePreferences, applyClonePreferences, and the preferencesFileAbs parameter of loadMergedSettings. settings.Load stops shelling out to git rev-parse --git-common-dir on every call (it does today, via clonePreferencesPathForWorktreeRoot, purely to find this file).
Repo key for repos without an origin
Reuse #2030's TrustIdentity rule exactly: origin present and every fetch/push URL normalizes → keyed by host/owner/repo; otherwise keyed by canonical worktree path. One rule, already documented, already tested for Windows drive letters and case folding.

Migration 3 — logs and tmp
Three candidate homes for .entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}; the choice is about layout, not trust, since all three are Entire-owned and gitignored or outside the tree.

A · Keep <worktree>/.entire/… for repo-enabled repos (status quo)
No migration; doctor bundle and docs unchanged. Cost: two layouts to reason about once #2030 lands (global repos use B), and the runtime dir sits inside a tree the repository controls, so it needs the #2154/#2156 guard forever.

B · <git-common>/entire/worktree/<key>/… for every active repo ← recommended
#2030 already builds this for global mode; adopting it for local mode gives one layout, one os.Root anchor, byte-clean git status in every repo, and takes runtime data out of the repository-controlled tier. Cost: a one-time move of existing logs (or just start fresh — full.jsonl is regenerated per Stop), and the temp file for an atomic write must be on the same filesystem as its destination (it will be — same .git).

C · ~/.local/state/entire/repos/<key>/… (XDG state; %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows)
Right for logs that are not about one repo (login, version check, the future session-binding records currently in ~/.config/entire/sessions/). Wrong for metadata/tmp: hooks would write across filesystems, and two clones of one repo would collide on the key.

So: B for repo runtime, C as a new userdirs.State() for the handful of things that are genuinely per-user (move sessions/ there from ~/.config — config directories should hold things a user might edit). doctor bundle learns both roots; doctor logs keeps its --worktree semantics by resolving through RuntimeRoot().

Windows checklist
Each item is a real failure mode seen in this repo's history or a documented platform difference; the convention is only worth having if these are encoded in the primitives, not remembered by reviewers.

Location. Keep config at %USERPROFILE%\.config\entire. It is non-idiomatic, but contexts.json and tokens.json are already there for every Windows user, and git-remote-entire reads the same path; moving it means a coordinated migration across two binaries for a cosmetic gain. New Data()/State() surfaces should use %LOCALAPPDATA%\entire as plugin_store.go already does. Document the asymmetry once in userdirs.
Permissions. 0600/0700 are no-ops; Chmod toggles read-only. EnsurePrivateDir already skips; ReadOwned's mode check must skip too. Privacy comes from the profile directory's inherited ACL, which is the norm for every other CLI (gh, aws, git).
Rename over an open file fails (ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION). Any concurrent reader — a second hook, Defender, an editor — makes WriteFileAtomic's rename fail. Retry with backoff (a few attempts over ~250 ms) inside the primitive; #455 was this in go-git's object store.
No directory fsync. Already best-effort; the branch's syncdir_windows.go whitelists ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION/ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED/ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. Keep that list in one place.
Locks leave .lock files behind. LockFileEx needs a real file; they already litter ~/.config/entire and .git/entire. Fine, but entire clean should know they are ours.
os.Root and junctions. A Root refuses to traverse an absolute symlink, and Windows junctions are reported as symlinks. A user whose ~/.config is a junction (Scoop users, OneDrive-redirected profiles) would get every user-tier read rejected if we anchored a Root above it. This is why the user tier resolves first, then opens, and never uses os.Root for its own files. The worktree tier keeps os.Root, where refusing junctions is the desired behaviour.
Reserved names and separators. os.Root rejects NUL, COM1… by itself; filepath.Join does not. paths.ValidateID is the one place that rejects them for plain joins, so an ID like con from a checkpoint can never create .entire/metadata/con.
Case folding. Repo keys and path exclusions fold on darwin/windows (repopolicy.caseInsensitivePaths); the repos map in the user file must be looked up with the same fold, or C:\Code\Cli and c:\code\cli become two entries.
MSYS/Git-Bash paths. Hooks run under Git for Windows' bash, which hands us /c/Users/...; paths.normalizeMSYSPath exists — every resolver that compares a hook-supplied path to a stored key must route through it.
Long paths. <git-common>\entire\worktree\<64-bit key>\metadata\<session>\tasks\<toolUseID>\agent-<id>.jsonl approaches MAX_PATH under a deep %USERPROFILE%. Go enables long-path awareness for \\?\-prefixed paths only when the manifest allows it; keep the key short (the branch already moved to 64-bit) and prefer opening through a Root handle, which sidesteps path-length limits for the relative part.
CI. #1843 added a Windows job; make safefile's tests the ones that exercise rename-under-open-handle, junction refusal in the worktree tier, and junction tolerance in the user tier, so the platform is tested where the rules live.
Decisions the team needs to make
Does OPF's enabled/categories stay team-level? Proposal says yes — what gets redacted before it leaves a machine is a policy the repo owner sets; only how the binary is found is per-machine. The alternative (everything user-level) means a teammate without OPF installed silently pushes un-filtered content; the fail-closed pre-push already handles "enabled but missing binary", which is the right outcome.
Per-block tolerant decoding of the user file vs. #2030's whole-file strictness. Needed before any key is added to the file, otherwise a nightly and a stable on one machine fight. Suggest folding it into the #2030 stack now, since that is where the loader lives.
Runtime layout B for repo-enabled repos. One layout is a real simplification but a visible change (.entire/logs disappears from worktrees; docs and doctor hints move). Could ship behind the global-tier work or as its own follow-up.
How hard to fence with lint. The os.UserHomeDir ban with an agent/** allow-list is cheap and catches the next stray resolver. Banning os.ReadFile in four packages is more work (many test helpers) but is what turns "please use the safe primitive" into something CI enforces, the way Worktree.Status is enforced today.
Where ~/.config/entire/sessions/ (#1959) should live. If userdirs.State() is added, land #1959 on it rather than migrating later.
Windows config location. Stay at ~\.config\entire (recommended) or migrate to %APPDATA% in lockstep across entire and git-remote-entire.
Suggested first PR
User-tier loader in settings (lifted from repopolicy/user_settings.go, per-block decode), safefile.ReadOwned/ReadConfined/WriteAtomic extracted from their current homes with no behaviour change, the os.UserHomeDir lint fence, and OPF command honored from the user file. Everything else layers on top, and that PR alone deletes the HEAD probe from the pre-push path.

Sources: cmd/entire/cli/settings/{settings,opf_command_trust}.go, internal/entireclient/userdirs, cmd/entire/cli/trail_context_cache.go, cmd/entire/cli/plugin_store.go, cmd/entire/cli/internal/flock, cmd/entire/cli/jsonutil/write.go; branch fix/global-takeover-migration: settings/repopolicy/*, settings/global.go, paths/invisible.go, docs/architecture/global-tracking.md; GHSA-hqjp-v5g5-vxvf, GHSA-2h46-9x5w-4wf7 (CVE-2026-57208); PRs #1365 #1449 #2030 #2154 #2156 #2163; go doc os.Root (go1.26.6).
